source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Ok, we can add it, thank you for the suggestion. Please feel free to suggest any other changes.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
I traced the USB nets in the KiCad and I think I found the cause. The
USBLC6-2SC6 ESD chip (U3) has pin 5 (VBUS) connected to GND instead of
+5V. The D+/D- routing itself looks correct: connector A6/B6/A7/B7,
through U3, to ESP GPIO20 (D+) / GPIO19 (D-).

execution.observed_behavior: The integrated boards did not enumerate, and inspection found the USB ESD device's VBUS pin connected to GND instead of +5V.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
For the proper fix so we keep the ESD protection: correct the symbol
so pin 5 (VBUS) goes to +5V and pin 2 to GND separately (not tied
together), keeping the D+/D- pass-through through U3. With a correctly
wired USBLC6 the protection is back and USB works. Does that match
what you'll change? No rush, I'll keep testing in the meantime.

value_updates.ground_connection: U3 pin 2 to GND on a separate net
value_updates.data_line_routing: D+ and D- pass through U3

execution.observed_behavior: Freelancer claims the requested USBLC6 symbol and wiring correction is fixed.

routing_warnings.description: The observed failure to enumerate is direct execution evidence for native USB operation; it is used here only as supporting context for the identified ESD wiring defect.
Removing U3 and bridging the data lines restored USB operation, verifying the native USB path while leaving the ESD-protection Requirement unsatisfied.
Enumeration and flashing after removing U3 and bridging the data lines verify native USB operation without verifying the required ESD protection.
